newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end broadly stable in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end broadly stable in low volume.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed broadly stable Tuesday in thin trade amid a lack of news to shake investors from their lethargy, brokers said.

The market will continue to see thin trade and mixed prices this week because as the seasonal lull is setting in earlier than usual this year. Players have resigned themselves to the economy not picking up until 1997, dealers said.
Tuesday, the General Index edged down 0.06 percent to 1,437.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index rose 0.23 percent to 2,050.1 points, according to preliminary figures.
In 1,500 trades, volume was 26.9 million soles ($10.4 million).
"While it is true the performance of the economy has been weak, investors are still looking at individual stocks," said Luis Caldern of local brokerage Acciones y Valores.

The only noteworthy activity during the largely apathetic session was the continued rebound of Telefnica del Per, lifted by price rises in New York, according to Augusto Lafora of the local brokerage Prisma. The benchmark climbed 1.37 percent to 5.18 soles on volume of 1.27 million shares.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, in which the government is selling a 30 percent stake this month, closed down 2.33 percent at 3.36 soles in low volume of 90,000 shares.
Brokers said they expect the government to set the sale price of its placement, scheduled for later Tuesday, between 3.40 and 3.45 soles per share.
